subject: Re: Operational approval request — enforce region-locked serving + no-fallback (PHI)
messages:
From: Amanda Lopez <amanda.lopez@horizonhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: HorizonHealth Legal <legal@horizonhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Request: enforce region-locked serving + no-fallback for PHI flows

Hi Irene & Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. HorizonHealth is ready to move to a pilot, but our security and compliance team has a non-negotiable requirement: any inference involving PHI must be served only in our US-only region and must not fall back to any other model variant or region under any circumstances.

Concretely, we need:
- Region lock to us-west-2 for all production inference for the pilot.
- A strict no-fallback policy (if the primary variant or capacity is unavailable, requests must fail rather than route to a different region/model).
- An operational runbook from Redwood showing how outages are surfaced and how rollbacks are performed.

We appreciate that this is a stricter posture than your default routing behavior. Please advise what information you need from our side (SLA exceptions, signatures, legal wording) and whether Redwood can produce a draft runbook we can review.

Amanda Lopez
Sr. InfoSec Program Manager | HorizonHealth
Amanda.Lopez@horizonhealth.com
(415) 555-2187

[Attachment: horizon-req-summary.pdf (pdf)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Lopez <amanda.lopez@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: enforce region-locked serving + no-fallback for PHI flows

Amanda — thanks for the clear ask and the urgency. Looping in Product (Lauren), and Platform Ops (Marcus) + Security product lead (Priyom) so we can scope feasibility and the approvals path.

A couple quick clarifying questions so we can draft a runbook and estimate lift:
1) Will Horizon require the no-fallback behavior at the router layer (immediate 503 on mismatch) or would a short retry window to the same region be acceptable if capacity is temporarily saturated?
2) Are you also asking for model pinning to a quantized variant (e.g., v1.2-q4) or is model choice flexible as long as it remains region-bound?
3) For telemetry and audit: do you need request-level logs stored for 7 years, or is 1-year retention sufficient for the pilot?

We'll prepare an operational runbook draft and a minimal risk analysis. Can you confirm legal contact for a potential SLA/exception signature?

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
[Attachment: initial-risk-analysis.xlsx]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: enforce region-locked serving + no-fallback for PHI flows

Thanks for pulling this in, Irene. High-level implications from Product/Platform:

- No-fallback hard lock: feasible, but it changes failure semantics for the customer. Instead of transparent failover we must return an explicit failure and surface it to the app. That will have availability implications; customers will see more 5xx/503s during regional incidents.
- Model pinning: we can support pinning to a specific model + quantization profile, but that increases operational overhead (separate serving pools).
- Telemetry: we can include per-request audit logs and export them to a customer-owned S3 bucket with 1/3/7-year retention options; retention beyond 1 year may require procurement changes.

Request to Security/Compliance: please draft a proposed operational runbook skeleton with the following sections so Legal/Customer can review quickly:
- Acceptance criteria and fail behavior (what we return on no-fallback)
- Monitoring & alerting thresholds (who gets paged)
- Manual escalation steps & rollback procedure
- Security controls & KMS/HSM boundaries

Priyom/Marcus — can Platform/Infra estimate effort and whether we need a dedicated pool in us-west-2 for the pilot? If so, what lead time and cost delta are we looking at?

I'll prepare a short customer-facing FAQ that explains availability tradeoffs.

LAUREN BISHOP
VP Product | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

From: Amanda Lopez <amanda.lopez@horizonhealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: HorizonHealth Legal <legal@horizonhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 11:09:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: enforce region-locked serving + no-fallback for PHI flows

Thanks, Lauren/Irene. We require immediate 503 behavior — retries to other regions are unacceptable. Model pinning: we prefer Redwood to pin to the validated model variant you recommend (we will sign off), so the ops burden is acceptable for our pilot.

Legal contact: Angela Chu (angela.chu@horizonhealth.com) — she'll handle SLA wording and e-signature. I attached a short legal note and the DocuSign request we usually use.

DocuSign: https://redwood.app/ds/DOCU-SIGN-4892

Best,
Amanda

[Attachment: horizon-legal-note.pdf]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 17:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: enforce region-locked serving + no-fallback for PHI flows

Priyom/Marcus — forwarding the confirmed customer posture. They want:

- Region lock to us-west-2 (customer-managed VPC or private link)
- Hard no-fallback behavior (return 503/failed call if primary is unavailable)
- Model pinning to our validated variant for the pilot (we select and they sign)
- Per-request audit logs exported to customer S3 (1 year retention for pilot)

Attachments included by customer: horizon-legal-note.pdf, and a DocuSign request link. I've attached our draft runbook (no-fallback-runbook-draft.pdf) and the risk analysis we mentioned. Please review and provide:
- Platform: estimate for dedicated pool + migration lead time and monthly cost delta.
- Security: gap analysis — does the runbook cover KMS/HSM boundaries and audit needs, and any compliance risks we should escalate?
- Product/Legal: suggested SLA exception language we can send to Angela Chu.

I will coordinate with Amanda for a Thursday call if needed.

Thanks,
Irene
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
[Attachment: no-fallback-runbook-draft.pdf]
